journey.title: Author a document from sourced facts and have it land in the corpus
journey.purpose: The write spine's equivalent of ingest-to-citation, and deliberately its mirror. A spec is authored against real sources, an agent adjusts it conversationally, it renders under a template, it switches template without re-authoring, and it ends where every document ends: in the corpus, citable, with a receipt saying where every step ran.

steps.intent: Pick a template and see what it can actually honor on the target you need, before writing anything.
Create a spec against that template. Content and intent only — the template decides how it looks.
Bind blocks to real sources — a corpus anchor, a project measure — so each figure traces to where it came from, and leave the voice blocks authored and visibly so.
Ask the agent to move a block to a different page. It edits the spec, not the rendered file, and the turn shows where its reasoning ran.
Render to the selected target. The default path makes no outbound call, so this costs nothing and leaves nothing.
Switch to a different template. Before it commits, see exactly which elements the new target cannot represent and which overrides it cannot honor — then decide.
Check where every step ran — parse, inference, render, and every agent turn — before the document goes anywhere that matters.
Find the generated document sitting in the corpus as an ordinary document: content-addressed, derived, anchored and searchable like anything that arrived from outside.

claims.statement: Switching template re-renders the document without asking the operator to re-supply any content.
claims.rationale: OT-P2-011. This is the payoff of persisting sources, spec and bindings separately: only bindings are discarded on a switch. A switch that re-asked for content would mean the layers were never really separate.

claims.statement: Every sourced block in the finished document can be traced back to the origin it was bound to, and authored blocks are distinguishable from sourced ones throughout.
claims.rationale: A generated report whose numbers cannot be traced is a claim, not a document. Allowing authored content and marking it is what lets one surface serve both a pitch deck and a research report.

claims.statement: Every conversational change lands as a spec version, and reverting to a prior version restores the document exactly.
claims.rationale: OT-P2-010 and OT-P2-021. If chat could edit rendered bytes, the artifact would diverge from the record explaining it and undo, diff and reproducibility would all quietly stop being correct.

claims.statement: The journey ends with a record showing where every step ran, including each agent turn and the render itself.
claims.rationale: OT-P2-023 and OT-P2-026. This is the read spine's wedge run backwards, and the agent turns are the part a user would otherwise assume was hosted. A receipt that covered parsing but not the conversation would be evidence for the wrong claim.

claims.statement: The generated document appears in the Corpus with the same affordances as an ingested one, and can be searched and cited identically.
claims.rationale: OT-P2-020. Generated documents are not a second class. Closing the loop back into the read spine is also what makes the round-trip fidelity gate a production path rather than only a test.
